question: E = p²/(2m). If % error in momentum p is 1% and % error in mass m is 2%, the % error in E is:
explanation:
E = p² × (2m)⁻¹ → power of p is 2, power of m is 1

ΔE/E = 2(Δp/p) + 1(Δm/m)

= 2(1%) + 1(2%) = 2% + 2% = **4%** ✓

(The constant 2 in denominator has no error. |power of m| = 1)
hint: Write E = p² × m⁻¹. Power of p = 2, power of m = 1. Apply error formula.

title: ⚡ JEE Shortcut: Max % Error in Any Formula
body:
For Z = AᵃBᵇ/CᶜDᵈ:

**% error in Z = a(%ΔA) + b(%ΔB) + c(%ΔC) + d(%ΔD)**

All terms POSITIVE (absolute powers). The variable with the HIGHEST power contributes the MOST error.

💡 Strategy: if two measurements have equal % error, the one raised to a higher power dominates.

quick.label: B³ gives 3× more error contribution than C¹ for same % error

question: R = V/I where V = (100 ± 2) V and I = (10 ± 0.5) A. The % error in R is:
hint: For R = V/I: relative errors add. Calculate % error in V and I separately, then add.

instruction: Match the formula to the correct error propagation rule:
explanation:
√A = A^(1/2) so power = 1/2 → ΔZ/Z = (1/2)(ΔA/A).
For Z = A − B: same rule as addition — ΔZ = ΔA + ΔB (errors add regardless of sign).

title: Significant Figures — What and Why

sections.heading: What Are Significant Figures?
sections.body:
Significant figures (SF or sig figs) are the **meaningful digits** in a measurement.

They reflect the precision of the measuring instrument:
• 3.46 cm (3 SF) → read to nearest 0.01 cm
• 3.4 cm (2 SF) → read to nearest 0.1 cm

sections.heading: Why It Matters in JEE
sections.body:
JEE Numerical Value questions and result expression require correct sig figs.

• Over-reporting: 2.5 × 3.1 = 7.75 → should be **7.8** (2 SF)
• Under-reporting: 2.50 × 3.10 = 7.75 → correct to **3 SF** = 7.75

highlight: Sig figs = precision of measurement. Never report more precision than your instrument provides.

title: Significant Figure Counting Rules
caption: Apply these rules in order. Scientific notation removes all ambiguity.
html:
RuleExampleSF
Non-zero digits: always significant3.463
Zeros between non-zeros: significant3.0464
Leading zeros: NOT significant0.00342
Trailing zeros after decimal: significant3.4604
Trailing zeros in integer: ambiguous34002,3 or 4
Scientific notation: all mantissa digits3.40×10³3
💡 Tip: Use scientific notation to remove all ambiguity about trailing zeros!

title: Tap to Reveal: Sig Fig Rules with Examples
instruction: Tap each rule to reveal examples.

items.back:
All non-zero digits are significant.
3.46 → 3 SF | 28.9 → 3 SF | 1234 → 4 SF

Zeros trapped between non-zero digits are significant.
3.046 → 4 SF | 1001 → 4 SF | 40.05 → 4 SF

Zeros to the LEFT of all non-zero digits: NOT significant.
0.0034 → 2 SF | 0.04 → 1 SF | 0.007 → 1 SF

Trailing zeros to the RIGHT of the decimal point ARE significant.
3.460 → 4 SF | 5.00 → 3 SF | 12.0 → 3 SF

Ambiguous without a decimal point.
3400 → could be 2, 3, or 4 SF
Write 3.40 × 10³ to show 3 SF clearly.

question: How many significant figures are in the number 0.00340?
explanation:
Breaking down 0.00340:
• '0.00' — leading zeros → NOT significant
• '3' → significant (non-zero digit)
• '4' → significant (non-zero digit)
• '0' — trailing zero after decimal → significant

Total = **3 significant figures** ✓

In scientific notation: 3.40 × 10⁻³ (3 SF is clear)
hint: Leading zeros (before the 3) are not significant. The trailing zero after 4 IS significant because it follows the decimal.

title: Sig Figs in Arithmetic Operations

sections.heading: Addition & Subtraction
sections.body:
Round result to the **least number of decimal places** among all numbers.

Example:
12.4 + 3.52 + 0.123 = 16.043
→ 12.4 has fewest decimal places (1)
→ Answer: **16.0** (1 decimal place)

sections.heading: Multiplication & Division
sections.body:
Round result to the **least number of significant figures** among all numbers.

Example:
2.5 × 3.14 = 7.85
→ 2.5 has fewest SF (2)
→ Answer: **7.9** (2 SF)

sections.heading: Rounding Rules
sections.body:
• Digit to drop < 5 → leave preceding digit unchanged
• Digit to drop > 5 → increase preceding digit by 1
• Digit to drop = 5 → round to even (2.45 → 2.4, 2.35 → 2.4)

highlight: Addition/Subtraction → match DECIMAL PLACES. Multiplication/Division → match SIG FIGS. Two different rules!

sentence: The result of 2.33 × 4.1 reported to the correct number of significant figures is _______.
explanation:
2.33 × 4.1 = 9.553

Sig figs: 2.33 has 3 SF, 4.1 has **2 SF** → answer must have 2 SF.

9.553 rounded to 2 SF = **9.6** ✓

(The '5' in 9.553 rounds up the 9.5 to 9.6)

title: ⚡ Order of Magnitude — Quick Concept
body:
Order of magnitude = the power of 10 nearest to the number.

Method:
1. Write in scientific notation: N × 10ᵖ
2. If N < √10 ≈ 3.162 → order = 10ᵖ
3. If N ≥ 3.162 → order = 10ᵖ⁺¹

Examples:
• 4500 = 4.5 × 10³ → 4.5 > 3.162 → order = 10⁴
• 2000 = 2.0 × 10³ → 2.0 < 3.162 → order = 10³

question: The result of (14.5 + 1.234 − 3.24) expressed to correct significant figures is:
explanation:
14.5 + 1.234 − 3.24 = 12.494

For addition/subtraction → match DECIMAL PLACES:
• 14.5 → **1 decimal place** (least)
• 1.234 → 3 decimal places
• 3.24 → 2 decimal places

Round 12.494 to 1 decimal place = **12.5** ✓
hint: For addition/subtraction: find which number has the fewest decimal places. Round the answer to match.
